data.title: Victory – a drawing and period reports on the Old Hungarians
data.excerpt: At the beginning of the 10th century our ancestors did not have an easy time: the power struggles of Svätopluk's sons, the Franks, and on top of that a new enemy, the nomadic Old Hungarians. Our collaborator Tomáš Humaj has drawn one of the brighter moments of that fighting, and period chronicles accompany the drawing.
data.metaTitle: Victory – a drawing and period reports from 889
data.metaDescription: A drawing accompanied by period reports on the arrival of the Hungarians in 889: how the Pechenegs drove them from their Scythian seats and how raids began.

blocks.text: In the year 889 from the Incarnation of the Lord, the nation of the Hungarians, the most savage of all and crueller than all monsters, unknown in past centuries because it was nowhere named, came forth from somewhere among the Scythian kingdoms and the marshes which the Don spreads out to infinity with its waters.
blocks.source: The Chronicle of Regino (for the year 889)

blocks.text: The aforementioned nation was thus driven out of its own seats by neighbouring nations which are called the Pechenegs, for these outweighed them both in numbers and in valour, and their native land, as we have already said, was not sufficient to accommodate the immense growth of the population. And so, when the Hungarians had been violently driven out by them, having taken leave of their homeland they set out to seek new lands which they might inhabit and in which they might establish their seats.
blocks.source: The Chronicle of Regino (for the year 889)

blocks.text: First they wander through the wildernesses of the Pannonians and the Avars, seeking their daily sustenance from hunting and fishing. Later they burst with frequent hostile raids into the regions of the Carantanians, the Moravians and the Bulgarians, killing few people with the sword but many thousands with the arrows which they loose with such skill from bows made of horn that it is hard to avoid being hit by them.
blocks.source: The Chronicle of Regino (for the year 889)

blocks.text: The year 902. The Hungarians attacked the territory of the Moravians. In the battle, however, they were defeated and took to flight.

children.text: Our ancestors did not have an easy time at the beginning of the 10th century. The power struggles of Svätopluk's sons, the Franks trying once again to subjugate the territory of Great Moravia, and on top of that a new enemy – the nomadic Old Hungarians. They had, it is true, concluded peace with King Svätopluk, but after his death it ceased to hold. The Slavs fought many battles with the Hungarians, some of them victorious, some of them sadly ending in defeat.
The scene that our collaborator Tomáš Humaj has drawn for us is one of the brighter moments (from the point of view of the Slavs). The drawing is called “VICTORY”
